lawyer: TH Khan with Gour Gopal Saha, Advocates ----- For the Accused-Appellant
parties:
Niranjan Deb ------ Accused-Appellant 
vs.
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
8. Mr. TH Khan, the learned Counsel, for the accused-appellant has seriously assailed the order or conviction on various grounds. He submits that the order of conviction is based on no evidence, the ingredients of sections 467/471/409 and section 5(2) of Act II, 1947 are totally lacking, the accused- appellant is a public servant but no sanction having been obtained from the Government for the prosecution of the accused-appellant the prosecution has been bad in law and he lastly, submits that the accused-appellant was made the scapegoat. 

 34. Section 2 of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947 provides that "For the purposes of this Act, Public Servant means a public servant as defined in section 21 of the Penal Code, and includes an employee of the Corporation or other body or organization set up by the Government and includes a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Member, Officer or other employee of a local authority, or a Chairman, Director, Managing Director, Trustee, Member, Officer or other employee of any corporation, or other body of organization constituted or established under any law." 

 35. The accused-appellant being an employee of a statutory corporation namely, Sonali Bank, was a 'Public Servant' at the relevant time as per the above definition. Further as per section 21 of the Penal Code and also under section 2(b) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958, the accused-appellant was a Public Servant. 

 36. Section 5(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 provides that "Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, or any other law, the offences specified in the schedule shall be triable exclusively by a Special Judge." And the offences punishable under section 409 of the Penal Code and the offences punishable under the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947 are so specified in the schedule to the Criminal Law Amendment Act. Accordingly, offences under section 409 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 are triable by a Special Judge alone. 

 37. Section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 provides that "Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898 or in any other law, previous sanction of the Government shall be required for the prosecution of a Public Servant for an offence under this Act and such sanction shall be sufficient for the prosecution of a Public Servant for an offence triable under this Act." From the evidence of the witnesses or from the records it does not appear that such sanction was obtained by the prosecution or by the Court. Such sanction was not even sought for. 

 38. Since no such sanction has been obtained or sought for, on this ground alone the trial has been vitiated. If sanction as required under section 6(5) Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 is not accorded by the government or is deemed not to have been so accorded as per proviso to sub-section 5 of section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958, the court shall have no jurisdiction to hold a trial against a public servant. This view of mine finds support from the decision in the case of Abdul Halim vs. State reported in 45 DLR 352 wherein it has been observed that if the sanction is invalid, the trial Court would not be a court of competent jurisdiction.
